summary: The merchant principality of the East Lands: houses, ledger and credit; the Stabilo Pact; hired companies; the three answers to the King of the East.

princes_household.name: The Prince's Household
princes_household.desc: A large, gilded household that every merchant's son wishes to join. It costs less than a war and wins more friends.

contract_courts_spirit.name: The Contract Courts
contract_courts_spirit.desc: Benches of sworn clerks settle disputes between merchants. A contract sealed in Postondoroth is worth what is written on it.

princes_purse_spirit.name: The Prince's Purse
princes_purse_spirit.desc: The prince holds the purse and decides quickly. The houses grumble and pay.

council_of_houses_spirit.name: The Council of Houses
council_of_houses_spirit.desc: The great houses govern together. Nothing is rushed, nothing is hidden, and the peace is rarely broken.

letters_of_credit_spirit.name: Letters of Credit
letters_of_credit_spirit.desc: A merchant carries a sealed letter in place of a purse. Robbers on the roads find the trade less rewarding.

great_ledger.name: The Great Ledger
great_ledger.desc: The ledgers of the East are bound in a single book, and its keepers know every debt and every debtor.

fortified_caravanserais_spirit.name: Fortified Caravanserais
fortified_caravanserais_spirit.desc: Towers and iron-bound gates guard the great caravanserais, and raiders find the walls awake.

prince_of_caravans.name: Prince of the Caravans
prince_of_caravans.desc: Every caravan on the southern roads carries a letter from Postondoroth, and the drivers call the prince by a title that is not yet official.

pact_council_spirit.name: The Pact Council
pact_council_spirit.desc: Delegates of the Pact settle their quarrels by arbitration in the hall of weights.

pact_garrisons_spirit.name: Pact Garrisons
pact_garrisons_spirit.desc: Small garrisons of every member drill together in the common fort and fight alongside one another.

shield_companies_spirit.name: The Shield-Companies
shield_companies_spirit.desc: Stabilo hires its armies, pays them on the day and keeps them well trained.

standing_companies_spirit.name: The Standing Companies
standing_companies_spirit.desc: The best companies hold permanent posts, keep their banners and are never disbanded.

contracts_of_service_spirit.name: Contracts of Service
contracts_of_service_spirit.desc: Every hireling is sworn on the same form, and the wounded are compensated by the same law.

desert_shield.name: The Desert Shield
desert_shield.desc: A line of forts, wells and towers runs along the edge of the dunes, and raiders find the shields of Postondoroth waiting.

temple_partners.name: Partners of the Temple Banks
temple_partners.desc: Temple silver flows into the prince's vaults, and relief houses open in the poor quarters.

princes_auditors.name: The Prince's Auditors
princes_auditors.desc: Sworn auditors count every temple and counting-house and report to the prince alone.

treasury_of_the_east.name: Treasury of the East
treasury_of_the_east.desc: Postondoroth pays the wages of the King of the East, and its ledgers are open to the throne.

kings_mint.name: The King's Mint
kings_mint.desc: The mint of Postondoroth strikes coin in the King's image and is trusted in every market of the East.

free_crowns_purse.name: The Free Crowns' Purse
free_crowns_purse.desc: The courts that refused the King of the East draw on the vaults of Postondoroth, and remember it.

free_roads.name: The Free Roads
free_roads.desc: The roads of the East belong to those who walk them, and the scales of Postondoroth weigh for every court alike.

princes_ambition.name: The Prince's Ambition
princes_ambition.desc: One prince, one ledger, one East. The houses have agreed to it, for now.

credit.name: Credit from Postondoroth
credit.desc: A loan from the bankers of Fudol eases the court's purse for a year. The ledger notes the day it falls due.

the_merchant_houses.title: The Merchant Houses
the_merchant_houses.desc: The great houses of Postondoroth sit around the table with the prince at its head. The treasurer asks, as she does each year, who will hold the keys of the vault.

the_houses_vote.title: The Houses Vote
the_houses_vote.desc: The stones are cast in the urn, and the clerk counts them aloud. Roads, credit and companies each have their patrons, and the prince will spend the year's silver where the count falls.

prince_and_houses.title: The Prince and the Houses
prince_and_houses.desc: The prince and the great houses have drawn up a charter of duties on a single sheet. Every seal is set to it, and the ink is still wet when the bells ring.

wells_of_obmi.title: The Wells of Obmi
wells_of_obmi.desc: Clerks of Postondoroth have come to Obmi with a lease of the central wells and an offer to share the tolls. The elders say that a lease is a rope with two ends.

friendship_of_drak.title: The Friendship of Drak
friendship_of_drak.desc: The prince of Postondoroth has sent Drak a gift and a reminder of the Pact. Drak is the oldest friend of the scales, and the oldest debtor.

options.name: Ask Postondoroth to forgive our debt.

letter_from_postondoroth.title: A Letter from Postondoroth
letter_from_postondoroth.desc: A courier in a grey cloak has brought Prince Blozan a letter bearing the scales of Postondoroth. It offers friendship, a place at the Pact table and, in the second paragraph, a loan.

mines_of_erco.title: The Mines of Erco
mines_of_erco.desc: Postondoroth offers to buy the copper and tin of Erco and to build a road to carry it. The mountain lords do not like to sell their ore for the promise of a road.

bargain_with_miaed.title: A Bargain with Miaed
bargain_with_miaed.desc: The merchants of Postondoroth ask the lords of Miaed to open the passes to Pact caravans, in exchange for protection against winter raiders. The lords weigh the offer.

options.name: Open the passes to Pact caravans.

marriage_in_the_pact.title: A Marriage in the Pact
marriage_in_the_pact.desc: Three houses offer a marriage to bind the Pact more firmly than any treaty. The prince's counsellors are divided, and the guests are already on the road.

options.name: A daughter of Drak's royal house.
A daughter of the House of Azano.

temple_accounts.title: The Temple Accounts
temple_accounts.desc: The temple banks of the Zilin Hills offer the prince a partnership in the caravan trade. Their envoys are courteous, and their ledgers are very orderly.

the_crowned_ledger.title: The Crowned Ledger
the_crowned_ledger.desc: On the counting-table of Postondoroth the prince is crowned with a circlet of melted coin. The houses file in one by one and lay their seals before him.

options.name: Long live the Prince of All Roads.

reckoning_of_the_east.title: The Reckoning of the East
reckoning_of_the_east.desc: The hall of weights is full. The rivalry with Furvior, the debts of the courts, the temples' footholds and the host on the rift are set out on the great table like goods at market. Every eye is on the prince.

loan_from_postondoroth.title: A Loan from Postondoroth
loan_from_postondoroth.desc: A banker of Fudol has called at the palace with a sealed offer. The sum is large, the interest is fair, and the repayment is written in a hand that looks very like a threat.

debt_called_in.title: Postondoroth Calls In a Debt
debt_called_in.desc: A polite clerk of Postondoroth stands at the gate with the ledger open to the right page. The debt is due, and he has all day to wait.

debtor_cannot_pay.title: A Debtor Cannot Pay
debtor_cannot_pay.desc: A court at the far end of the ledger has missed its payment for the third time. The clerks bring the file to the prince, and the prince wishes to hear all opinions before he chooses a mercy.

court_defaults.title: A Court Defaults
court_defaults.desc: The debtor has refused to pay and sent no explanation. The ledger records the default, and the clerks quietly note which roads the defaulter holds.

obmi_leased.title: Obmi's Answer
obmi_leased.desc: The elders of Obmi have leased the wells of the central road to Postondoroth. The first caravan of the Pact waters there before the month is out.

drak_answer.title: Drak's Answer
drak_answer.desc: A rider returns from Drak with a sealed reply. The old friendship is as warm as ever, and the old debt is as old as ever.

plutondo_answer.title: Plutondo's Answer
plutondo_answer.desc: Prince Blozan's answer arrives in a gilded case. It is courteous, long and not entirely clear.

erco_sold.title: Erco's Answer
erco_sold.desc: The mountain lords of Erco have agreed to sell their ore to the Pact. The first string of mules comes down the mountain a week later.

miaed_opened.title: Miaed's Answer
miaed_opened.desc: The lords of Miaed have opened the passes. Caravans of the Pact will cross the snow-line in winter, and pay the toll in silver.

obmi_refused.title: Obmi Keeps Its Wells
obmi_refused.desc: The elders of Obmi have returned the lease unsealed. The wells are theirs, they say, and the Pact may dig its own.

erco_refused.title: Erco Keeps Its Ore
erco_refused.desc: The mountain lords of Erco have sent back the prince's offer with a lump of raw copper and a polite refusal.

miaed_closed.title: The Passes Stay Closed
miaed_closed.desc: The lords of Miaed have turned the Pact's merchants away. Snow is already deep in the passes, and they intend to keep it so.

focuses.name: The Merchant Houses
focuses.desc: Postondoroth is a city of counting-tables, and its prince reigns because the great houses agree to let him. Prince Cereos has asked the houses who keeps the keys.

focuses.name: The Prince of Postondoroth
focuses.desc: The prince's household is large, gilded and expensive, and every merchant of the city wants a son in it. Its upkeep is cheaper than a war.

focuses.name: The House of Azano
focuses.desc: Lady Mylun Azano keeps the treasury of the principality. Her books are said to be honest, and nobody has yet proved it otherwise.

focuses.name: The Seat at Postondoroth
focuses.desc: The old seat of the princes is repaired and rebuilt. Marble floors, a hall of weights and measures, and a vault with three locks.

focuses.name: The Contract Courts
focuses.desc: Disputes between merchants are settled before a bench of sworn clerks, not before the prince. A contract in Postondoroth is worth what is written on it.

focuses.name: The House of Shindor
focuses.desc: Captain-General Hardfic Shindor holds the contracts of the shield-companies. His house is paid in advance and its debtors are never late.

focuses.name: The Guild of Scales
focuses.desc: The Guild of Scales sets the weights and measures of every road. A false weight is punished by the loss of the right to trade.

focuses.name: The Prince's Purse
focuses.desc: The prince holds the purse and the houses advise. Decisions are made quickly, and the houses remember who made them.

focuses.name: The Council of Houses
focuses.desc: The great houses sit as a council and the prince sits among them. Nothing is decided without a majority of seals, and so nothing is decided in haste.

focuses.name: The Minted Crowns
focuses.desc: A new mint rings day and night, and the coin of Postondoroth is taken at face value in every market of the East. Its prince has his likeness stamped on every piece.

focuses.name: The Law of the Scales
focuses.desc: The Guild's rules are written into law. Courts, markets and harbours follow one measure, and the quarrels that once troubled the city grow rare.

focuses.name: The Houses Vote
focuses.desc: Once a year the houses cast their stones in the urn and decide where the principality will spend its silver. The count is long, and the prince listens to every stone.

focuses.name: The Hall of the Golden Ledger
focuses.desc: A great hall of white stone houses the ledgers of the principality, ten thousand volumes on cedar shelves. Clerks copy them out in triplicate.

focuses.name: The Pact Council Sits
focuses.desc: Representatives of the Stabilo Pact gather at Postondoroth for the first time. They sit in the hall of weights and are served the same wine.

focuses.name: The Prince and the Houses
focuses.desc: The prince and the houses sign a charter of duties on a single sheet. For the first time in a generation the principality speaks with one voice.

focuses.name: The Ledger of the East
focuses.desc: The bankers of Fudol open a ledger with the name of every eastern court at the top of a page. Some of the courts do not yet know they are in it.

focuses.name: The Bankers of Fudol
focuses.desc: Fudol is the oldest banking town of the East. Its bankers take deposits in gold, silver and salt and pay out in letters that are honoured from the rift to the dunes.

focuses.name: Letters of Credit
focuses.desc: A merchant carries a sealed letter in place of a purse, and a banker in a distant city pays him on sight. Robbers on the roads find the trade less rewarding.

focuses.name: Loans to the Kings
focuses.desc: The ledger now has room for kings. The Great Loan is offered only to courts with large lands and larger pride, who rarely read the terms.

focuses.name: The Counting Houses
focuses.desc: Counting houses open in every city of the principality, each with a vault, a clerk and a man with a sword. Interest accrues, and the prince is pleased.

focuses.name: Caravan Insurance
focuses.desc: A caravan that pays the Guild of Scales a small fee is repaid in full if it is robbed. The roads grow busier, and the Guild's ledgers fatter.

focuses.name: Collect the Debts
focuses.desc: A debtor who does not pay is visited by a polite clerk, then by a less polite one. The ledger records everything and forgives nothing.

focuses.name: The Interest of Peace
focuses.desc: A war empties the vault and brings no interest. The bankers of Fudol will lend to either side of a quarrel but profit most when there is none.

focuses.name: Debts Paid in Iron
focuses.desc: A court that cannot pay in coin may pay in arms. Wagon-loads of spears, shields and mail roll into the arsenals of Fudol, and the debt is struck from the page.

focuses.name: Rivals of the Temple Banks
focuses.desc: The temples lend as freely as the bankers, and they do not charge interest. Postondoroth quietly lets it be known that charity has a price too.

effects.tooltip: Courts in Postondoroth's debt listen less to the temples' friends.

focuses.name: Credit for the Rift Ports
focuses.desc: Postondoroth lends silver to the port-masters of the rift sea, secured against their harbour dues. A harbour in debt is a harbour that remembers its friends.

focuses.name: The Great Ledger
focuses.desc: The ledgers of the East are merged into one volume, bound in indigo leather and kept under three locks. It is said that a king may be ruined by a single page.

focuses.name: Creditor of Kings
focuses.desc: Four crowns of the East owe Postondoroth more than they can ever repay. The prince does not say it aloud, but the whole East knows it.

focuses.name: The Southern Roads
focuses.desc: Postondoroth was founded on the Gold Road, and its first prince was a toll-keeper. The caravans of the south have not forgotten it.

focuses.name: Caravanserais of the Gold Road
focuses.desc: Walled yards with cisterns, stables and sleeping galleries mark each day's journey along the Gold Road. The prince's seal on the gate is a promise of a roof and a clean well.

focuses.name: The Sand Road Charter
focuses.desc: Beyond the last cairn, the Sand Road runs south through the dunes. Postondoroth drafts a charter to guard it and invites the desert courts to sign.

focuses.name: West to Alerhia
focuses.desc: West of the Gold Road lie Alerhia, Kersian and Azano, rich in grain and short of silver. Postondoroth is happy to lend.

focuses.name: The Wells of Obmi
focuses.desc: Obmi holds the wells on the central Sand Road. The prince offers a lease of the wells in return for a share of the tolls.

focuses.name: Desert Patrols
focuses.desc: Riders in hired livery patrol the dunes in pairs, mapping the wells and guiding lost caravans to the road. Their pay is high, and their reports are accurate.

focuses.name: The Markets of The Moco
focuses.desc: The Moco lies at the lake end of the Gold Road, and its markets have never been fully served. Postondoroth buys stalls, warehouses and debts.

focuses.name: Trade of the South Lands
focuses.desc: The courts of the south sell dyes, spices and the sweet resin of their trees. Postondoroth offers to buy them all, on delivery, at a fair price.

focuses.name: A Bid for the Rift Road
focuses.desc: The Rift Road has long been Noris's, but its charter lapses at the next reckoning. Postondoroth sends its best advocates to Delbiz and its heaviest purses with them.

focuses.name: Fortified Caravanserais
focuses.desc: Towers are raised over the great caravanserais of the Gold Road, and the gates are fitted with iron. A raider who approaches finds the guards awake.

focuses.name: Beyond the Dunes
focuses.desc: A caravan commissioned by the Guild of Scales walks into the deep sand with a year's supply of water. The clerks record its departure and wait.

focuses.name: Prince of the Caravans
focuses.desc: Every caravan on the Gold, Sand and Lake Roads carries a letter from Postondoroth. The drivers call the prince by a title that is not yet official.

focuses.name: The Stabilo Pact
focuses.desc: The Pact binds Postondoroth and Drak to open roads, shared tariffs and a common watch. Its seal is a pair of scales held by a single hand.

focuses.name: The Friendship of Drak
focuses.desc: Drak is the oldest friend of the Pact and its oldest debtor. The prince sends a gift and a reminder.

focuses.name: Envoys of the Pact
focuses.desc: Envoys in grey travelling-cloaks set out for the courts of the East with sample cloths, letters of credit and a polite proposal.

focuses.name: The Pact Council
focuses.desc: Representatives of the Pact meet in the hall of weights and settle their quarrels by arbitration. No member may draw a blade in the hall.

focuses.name: A Letter to Prince Blozan
focuses.desc: Prince Blozan of Plutondo is young, ambitious and short of silver. A friendly letter from Postondoroth, with a draft attached, is likely to be welcome.

focuses.name: The Mines of Erco
focuses.desc: Erco's mountains hold copper and tin, and its prince has no way to bring them down. A road and a loan, offered together, may buy a friend.

focuses.name: Open the Pact
focuses.desc: The Pact has been a friendship of two. Now Postondoroth opens its doors and invites every eastern court that wants to weigh its goods on the prince's scales.

focuses.name: Oreton and the Red Lands
focuses.desc: Oreton and the Avalon hills trade red clay, copper bowls and dyed wool. Postondoroth maps the roads and offers to carry the goods to market.

focuses.name: A Bargain with Miaed
focuses.desc: The lords of Miaed hold the high passes between the dunes and the lakes. A bargain with them would open the roads in winter.

focuses.name: Pact Garrisons
focuses.desc: Each member of the Pact keeps a small garrison in the common fort at Postondoroth. They drill together, eat together and fight alongside one another.

focuses.name: A Marriage in the Pact
focuses.desc: A marriage between houses ties the Pact more firmly than any treaty. Three courts have offered daughters and dowries, and the prince must choose.

focuses.name: The Mountain Road to Erco
focuses.desc: A paved road is cut through the mountains to Erco, and mule-strings are replaced by wagons. The ore comes down cheaper, and Erco learns who paid for the road.

focuses.name: The Pact of Equals
focuses.desc: Each court of the Pact sits at the same table and speaks in turn. Postondoroth asks for the first cup and for no other privilege.

focuses.name: The Pact Under the Prince
focuses.desc: Protection contracts are drafted for every court that wishes one. The prince will defend them, and they will pay him a fixed tenth.

focuses.name: The Greater Pact
focuses.desc: The Pact is rewritten and sealed by every member. Gifts pass from hand to hand, and the debts of the weakest are forgiven in part. The whole table is satisfied.

focuses.name: The Shield-Companies
focuses.desc: Stabilo does not raise armies, it hires them. The shield-companies march under contract, are paid on the day, and are the best-trained troops in the East.

focuses.name: Hire the Sellswords
focuses.desc: A recruiting table stands in the market-square of Postondoroth. Any man with a sword and a clean record may sign for a year's service at triple pay.

focuses.name: Captain-General Hardfic Shindor
focuses.desc: Hardfic Shindor has led hired companies for forty years and has never broken a contract. The prince names him Captain-General, and the companies cheer louder than the pay requires.

focuses.name: Contracts of Service
focuses.desc: Every contract is now written on the same form, with the same oaths and the same compensation for the wounded. The companies know their rights and stand firm for them.

focuses.name: The Arsenal of Fudol
focuses.desc: Fudol's arsenal is rebuilt around a central armoury and a dozen new forges. A company paid in the morning is armed by the afternoon.

focuses.name: Forts on the Noris March
focuses.desc: Walls rise along the border where the lands of Postondoroth meet the lands of Furvior. The watchmen hired to man them are paid by the tower.

focuses.name: Paid in Full
focuses.desc: The companies are paid in full, and the prince adds arms to the wages. Rarely has the East seen a better-equipped hireling.

focuses.name: The Pikes of Postondoroth
focuses.desc: The pikemen of the shield-companies march in blocks of a hundred, with spears three men long. A cavalry charge breaks against them like the sea on rock.

focuses.name: Foreign Captains
focuses.desc: Captains from the far west, the ember lands and the cold north are paid to teach the companies their arts. They come for the silver and stay for the wine.

focuses.name: Siege Engineers
focuses.desc: Engineers from half a dozen lands are hired to design walls that cannot be scaled and engines that can scale any wall. Their drawings fill a room.

focuses.name: The Desert Shield
focuses.desc: A line of forts, wells and watch-towers runs along the edge of the dunes. A raider who reaches it finds the shields of Postondoroth already waiting.

focuses.name: The Standing Companies
focuses.desc: The best companies are offered permanent posts at higher pay. They keep their arms, their captains and their banners, and they are never disbanded.

focuses.name: The War Chest of the Pact
focuses.desc: The treasurers of the Pact count out coin for a war that nobody has yet declared. It is stored in iron-bound chests beneath the hall of weights.

focuses.name: The Army of the Pact
focuses.desc: The Pact calls out all its companies, and the roads are full of shields. A host such as the East has never seen marches out of Postondoroth.

focuses.name: The Temple Accounts
focuses.desc: The envoys of the Zilin Hills have asked to see the prince's books. They offer, in return, a partnership in the caravan trade.

focuses.name: Partners of the Temple Banks
focuses.desc: The prince makes the temple banks partners in the caravan trade. Their silver flows into his vaults, and his accounts become part of theirs.

focuses.name: Audit the Temples
focuses.desc: The prince's auditors open the temple ledgers and read them line by line. What they find, they keep to themselves.

focuses.name: The Relief Houses of Fudol
focuses.desc: Houses of relief open in Fudol, funded half by the temple banks and half by the prince. Hunger and fever are rarer in the quarter where they stand.

focuses.name: The Prince's Auditors
focuses.desc: A company of sworn auditors is sent to every temple and counting-house in the principality. They count, they cross-check, and they report to the prince alone.

focuses.name: Temple Loans for the Roads
focuses.desc: The temples offer silver for the roads, on terms the clerks find too generous. The prince reads the contract slowly, twice.

focuses.name: Close the Books to the Temples
focuses.desc: The temple clerks are barred from the counting-houses, and the debtors of Postondoroth are told to pay in coin of the prince's mint.

focuses.name: Faith and Interest
focuses.desc: Faith and interest sit at the same table in Postondoroth, and neither is permitted to speak first. The prince keeps both accounts.

focuses.name: The Reckoning of the East
focuses.desc: A king calls himself the Deliverer, and an army waits on the rift. The ledger of the East has never held a question like this one.

focuses.name: Treasurer of the East
focuses.desc: The generous friends in Postondoroth have offered the prince a new partnership. Stabilo pledges its ledgers to the Deliverer's cause.

focuses.name: Gold for the Deliverer
focuses.desc: The prince empties a vault into temple chests. Within the month, the temples have repaid the favour with promises, which he finds more durable than coin.

focuses.name: Contracts with the Temple
focuses.desc: A hundred contracts are drawn between the counting-houses of Postondoroth and the temple banks of the Zilin Hills. Each is worth more than the paper.

focuses.name: Kneel with Open Ledgers
focuses.desc: The prince lays his ledgers on the temple altar, open to the last page. He kneels before the King of the East, and the books are signed.

focuses.name: Paymaster of the Eastern Host
focuses.desc: The wages of the eastern host are paid from Postondoroth. The arms follow, wagon by wagon, with a clerk to count each spear.

focuses.name: The Debts of the Refusers
focuses.desc: Courts that refused the King of the East still owe Postondoroth. The prince, now the King's own creditor, calls the debts in.

focuses.name: The King's Mint
focuses.desc: The mint of Postondoroth strikes coin in the King's image. It is the only mint of the East that is trusted in every market.

focuses.name: Close the King's Books
focuses.desc: The King is dead, and his accounts are open at last. The clerks of Postondoroth go through them, line by line, to find who owes what to whom.

effects.tooltip: Postondoroth must answer for its loans.

focuses.name: Paymaster of the Free Crowns
focuses.desc: The prince refuses the King of the East and offers his purse to those who do the same. The Free Crowns will not want for silver.

focuses.name: Close the Temple Accounts
focuses.desc: The temple accounts are closed, the temple clerks are sent home, and the houses that served them are shut. The prince has read what was in the books.

focuses.name: Subsidies for the Courts
focuses.desc: Silver flows from Postondoroth to the courts that stand against the King of the East. In return, their ledgers are opened and their debts eased.

focuses.name: Arms for the Elder Groves
focuses.desc: Crates of spears, bows and mail are shipped across the rift to the forests of the elves. The prince sends them without being asked and without a bill.

focuses.name: The Free Crowns' Purse
focuses.desc: The courts that refused the King of the East gather at Postondoroth. The prince opens his vault, and the banner of the Free Crowns is raised over his counting-table.

focuses.name: Buy Off the Coalition
focuses.desc: Gold and promises pass between the camps of the coalition. By season's end, half its captains have remembered debts they owe at home.

focuses.name: War for the Free Crowns
focuses.desc: The companies of Stabilo are hired to fight for the Free Crowns. The prince offers a bonus for every day that the King's banner does not fly.

focuses.name: Companies for the Stranger
focuses.desc: A band of Stabilo's hired companies, paid in advance and unconcerned by politics, takes service with the stranger's coalition. The prince sees no reason to stop them.

focuses.name: The Free Roads
focuses.desc: The King of the East is gone, or his claim is not heard. The roads of the East belong again to those who walk them, and the scales of Postondoroth weigh for every court alike.

effects.tooltip: An outcome of this game, not history.

focuses.name: The Prince of All Roads
focuses.desc: Why should the East be ruled by a sword when it can be ruled by a contract? The prince resolves to buy every charter, sign every court and wear one crown.

focuses.name: Buy the Charters
focuses.desc: The charters of the roads are bought one by one, at prices that make the sellers rich and the buyer richer.

focuses.name: Protection Contracts
focuses.desc: A form is drawn up in two columns. On one side, the protection of Postondoroth. On the other, a tenth of every harvest.

effects.tooltip: Courts at lean 60 may be offered protection.

focuses.name: Vassals by Contract
focuses.desc: A court whose debt cannot be paid is offered a choice: the debtor's chains, or the protector's banner. Few read the small print.

focuses.name: The Crowned Ledger
focuses.desc: The prince is crowned on the counting-table of Postondoroth with a circlet made from melted coin. The houses applaud, and the ledger is bound in gold.

focuses.name: The Prince's Due
focuses.desc: The prince claims what is owed him, and his writ runs against the rival of the East. Clerks and companies set out together.

focuses.name: The Great Kingdoms Sign
focuses.desc: Envoys carry the prince's charter to Alerhia, Miaed, Erco and Plutondo. Each court must sign, or explain to the ledger why it will not.

focuses.name: No Credit for a God-King
focuses.desc: Not one coin will be lent to the King of the East, and no merchant of Postondoroth will weigh his goods. The prince has closed the ledger against him.

focuses.name: One East Under Postondoroth
focuses.desc: The roads, the courts and the debts of the East all end at Postondoroth. One prince sits on the counting-table of the East, and no court is outside his ledger.

effects.tooltip: An outcome of this game, not history.

focuses.name: Close the Roads to Noris
focuses.desc: Tolls rise, wells close and the riders of Furvior are turned back at the border. It is the first step toward the Caravan War.

focuses.name: Seize the Salt Road
focuses.desc: The companies of Postondoroth ride the Salt Road under the prince's writ. Every well and caravanserai on it is claimed for the ledger.

focuses.name: Terms at Postondoroth
focuses.desc: With the Salt Road in its hands, Postondoroth offers terms. The Caravan War may end with a handshake and a contract.

focuses.name: Answer the Eastern Coalition
focuses.desc: Stabilo has joined the eastern coalition. The companies cross the rift in hired boats, and the clerks go with them.

focuses.name: Spoils for the Ledger
focuses.desc: The taken groves are valued by the prince's assessors and entered in the ledger. Every harvest brings a portion home.

focuses.name: The Road to Parim
focuses.desc: The coalition turns west toward Parim, and the companies of Stabilo march at its head. The Golden City is within sight, and the contract is for its sack.

focuses.name: Call Back the Companies
focuses.desc: The war is no longer profitable, and the coin has run dry. The prince recalls the companies across the rift, though some contracts will never be paid.

effects.tooltip: Some contracts will never be paid.
